newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PRAISE ALL ROUND AFTER DAZZLING DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PRAISE ALL ROUND AFTER DAZZLING DRAW.

text.p: Italian coach Cesare Maldini and his Brazilian counterpart Mario Zagallo each praised the other's players after their incredible 3-3 draw in the Tournoi de France on Sunday.

Maldini, almost as animated on the touchline as his players were on the field, said the match was "an absolutely fantastic occasion, a true spectacle and one that Brazil did well to rescue from defeat".

He also praised his own players, saying: "Each and every one of them gave their all. I was very impressed with Filippo Inzaghi. He's the top scorer in Italy this season and came on for his debut and made a very good impression."
Zagallo was equally magnanimous to the Italians. "They showed tonight just what a great team they can be. I think that both sides showed they are well on course for the World Cup next year."

Alessandro Del Piero, who scored twice, once from the penalty spot as Italy led 2-0 and then 3-1, said: "That was a very tough game which neither team wanted to lose and I thought we were on our way to victory after we went 3-1 ahead.
"But Brazil are so powerful and dangerous coming forward, you can take nothing for granted. Still it was a great game to play in."

Ronaldo, who will soon be facing some of the Italian players on a regular basis when he completes his move from Barcelona to Inter Milan, was man-marked throughout by Fabio Cannavaro -- but still managed to squeeze home Brazil's second goal with 19 minutes to play.
"It was a tough experience," said the 20-year-old Brazilian. "Italian defenders are tougher, more disciplined and harder than Spanish defenders.
"This was the toughest match in the Tournoi so far, it was a game neither team wanted to lose and was the most fiercely competitive of all four games so far."
Cannavaro said: "My job was to stick as closely as possible to him, and until he scored I thought I was doing okay. Right now I am utterly exhausted chasing him all over the field."

Italian midfielder Christian Panucci said: "We played extremely well in the first half, but Brazil gradually came back into it. At the moment I would have to say they are mentally and physically superior than us."
Sunday's match was the 12th between the teams -- and maintained the parity between them. Both have won five times and drawn twice -- with a goal tally of 19-19.

Despite that record Brazil have beaten the Italians in the finals of the 1970 and 1994 World Cups -- and this was their first meeting since USA '94 when Brazil won on penalties at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena.
It looked as though Italy were on their way to gaining a small measure of revenge for that defeat, but two inspired goals from Ronaldo and Romario changed all that.
The result left England as winners of the tournament after beating Italy 2-0 and France 1-0 in their opening matches.
The tournament wraps up this week when England play Brazil on Tuesday and France meet Italy on Wednesday.
